s: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act relates to which of the following?
o: Reservation of 50% seats in private schools for all children
Reservation of 25% seats in all government colleges for girls
Reservation of 25% entry-level seats in unaided private schools for specified children
Reservation of 35% seats in aided schools for minorities
x: Section 12(1)(c) requires unaided private schools, excluding minority institutions, to reserve 25% of entry-level seats for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups.
tq: Identify the exact statutory provision by matching its percentage and institutional coverage.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to the 25% quota under Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, consider the following statements:
1. It applies to entry-level seats.
2. Minority institutions are excluded from its coverage.
3. The State reimburses schools on the basis of per-child expenditure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The provision concerns entry-level seats in unaided private schools, excludes minority institutions, and provides reimbursement by the State on a per-child expenditure basis.
tq: Test the provision through its seat level, institutional exception and reimbursement mechanism.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s: The pupil-teacher ratio prescribed under the RTE norms is correctly matched as:
x: The prescribed pupil-teacher ratio is 30:1 at the primary level and 35:1 at the upper-primary level.
tq: Read the comparison in level-wise order and avoid reversing the two ratios.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s: Which authority lays down the minimum qualifications for appointment of teachers under the RTE framework?
o: State Council for Teacher Education alone
National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
x: The minimum teacher qualifications are laid down by the academic authority notified by the Central Government, namely the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).
tq: Apply the 'who performs this function?' method to distinguish the national academic authority from monitoring bodies.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s: Teacher Eligibility Test under the RTE framework is conducted in accordance with guidelines of the:
x: Teacher Eligibility Test requirements operate according to guidelines issued by the NCTE.
tq: Separate teacher-qualification authority from child-rights monitoring institutions.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding detention under the RTE Act:
1. The original Act barred detention up to Class VIII.
2. The 2019 amendment permitted detention at certain stages subject to safeguards.
3. Re-examination is one of the safeguards associated with detention under the amended provision.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The original no-detention provision extended up to Class VIII, while the 2019 amendment allowed detention at Classes V and VIII after regular examinations and a re-examination opportunity.
tq: Track the change from the original rule to the amended rule and its safeguard.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s: Under the amended no-detention framework, detention may be permitted at which stages, subject to safeguards?
x: The 2019 amendment permits detention at Classes V and VIII, subject to regular examination, re-examination and related safeguards.
tq: Focus on the exact class numbers rather than the broad phrase 'elementary education'.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s: The provision relating to School Management Committees under the RTE Act is found in:
x: School Management Committees are provided for under Section 21 of the RTE Act.
tq: Match the institutional mechanism with its statutory section.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s: In every government or aided school, what proportion of the members of the School Management Committee are parents or guardians?
x: Three-fourths of the members of the School Management Committee are parents or guardians.
tq: Test the exact composition percentage and reject the extreme claim that all members must be parents.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following bodies are associated with monitoring and grievance redressal under the RTE Act?
1. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
2. State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights
3. School Management Committees as statutory monitoring commissions
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: NCPCR and SCPCRs review, monitor and redress grievances under the RTE Act. School Management Committees are school-level bodies, not statutory child-rights commissions.
tq: Distinguish formal commissions from school-level participatory bodies.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about the 86th Constitutional Amendment:
1. It inserted Article 21A.
2. It rewrote Article 45 to address early childhood care up to six years.
3. It added Article 51A(k).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A, revised Article 45 regarding early childhood care up to six years, and added the parental duty in Article 51A(k).
tq: Use the three-part amendment bundle rather than treating Article 21A as its sole effect.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT included within the principal coverage of the RTE Act as described?
o: Establishment of neighbourhood schools by the appropriate Government and local authority
Education at the pre-school and secondary levels as a statutory entitlement under the Act
A duty of parents or guardians to send the child to school
Free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years
x: The RTE Act does not include pre-school education below six years or secondary and higher education within its principal statutory entitlement.
tq: Find the option that extends the Act beyond its stated age and educational-stage coverage.
sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT a correct feature of the RTE Act?
o: The Centre bears the sole financial responsibility for implementing the Act.
Parents or guardians have a duty to send the child to school.
The appropriate Government and local authority must establish neighbourhood schools.
Unaided private schools provide specified entry-level seats for weaker and disadvantaged groups.
x: The Centre does not bear sole financial responsibility; funds are shared by the Centre and the States. The other statements describe features of the Act.
tq: Identify the false financial-responsibility claim hidden among genuine statutory duties.
sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the RTE Act?
1. Screening and capitation fee — prohibited
2. Physical punishment and mental harassment — prohibited
3. Private tuition by teachers — prohibited
4. Out-of-school child — admission to an age-appropriate class
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four are features of the RTE Act: it prohibits screening and capitation fee, physical punishment, mental harassment and private tuition by teachers, and provides age-appropriate admission for out-of-school children.
tq: Combine several statutory safeguards and inclusion measures before selecting the coded option.
sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. RTE Act — prohibition of capitation fee
2. Article 51A(k) — duty of parent or guardian regarding education
3. Section 12(1)(c) — 25% provision in unaided private schools
4. Section 21 — School Management Committees
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four pairings are correct. They connect the RTE Act's safeguards and institutions with the relevant constitutional provisions and sections.
tq: Start with the sure section matches and verify each remaining constitutional or statutory pairing.
sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

s: The Right to Education Act does NOT provide for coverage of which category under the 25% quota?
o: Children in minority institutions covered compulsorily by Section 12(1)(c)
Children in unaided private schools, subject to the provision
x: Minority institutions are excluded from the 25% quota provision under Section 12(1)(c). The provision concerns specified children in unaided private schools.
tq: Look for the institutional exception in a provision that otherwise appears broadly applicable.
sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

s: The cost-sharing pattern mentioned for Samagra Shiksha is correctly stated as:
o: 100:0 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States
40:60 generally and 10:90 for North-Eastern and hill States
60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States
50:50 generally and 75:25 for North-Eastern and hill States
x: The Centre-State sharing pattern is 60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States.
tq: Test both parts of a funding ratio and watch for reversed shares.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s:
The Supreme Court direction mentioned in relation to Section 12(1)(c) in January 2026 concerned which combination?
1. Framing of rules under Section 38
2. Monitoring by the NCPCR
3. Abolition of the 25% quota
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The January 2026 direction concerned rules under Section 38 and NCPCR monitoring. It did not abolish the 25% quota.
tq: Reject the extreme negative option and isolate the two linked institutional directions.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s: According to the current figure specified, the 25% quota under Section 12(1)(c) operates in how many States and Union Territories?
x: The specified current figure is 16 States and Union Territories.
tq: Treat the current count as a distinct quantitative fact and avoid estimating from the total number of States and Union Territories.
sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

s: The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on:
x: The UN General Assembly adopted the UNCRC on 20 November 1989.
tq: Separate the adoption date from India’s accession date and the dates of the Optional Protocols.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s: India’s accession to the UNCRC entails submission of periodic reports to the:
o: UN Committee on the Rights of the Child
x: States parties submit periodic reports to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child.
tq: Match the reporting obligation with the specialised treaty-monitoring committee.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four broad categories of rights under the UNCRC?
x: The four categories are survival, development, protection and participation. Sovereignty is not one of the UNCRC rights categories.
tq: Identify the outsider by recalling the four-category classification.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following rights:
1. Right to development
2. Right to expression
3. Right to recreation
Which of the above are recognised as child rights under the UNCRC framework?
x: Right to development, expression and recreation are all recognised as child rights within the UNCRC framework.
tq: Avoid treating the four broad categories as an exhaustive list of individual rights.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four core principles of the UNCRC?
o: Compulsory state ownership of all child institutions
Right to life, survival and development
x: The four core principles include non-discrimination, best interests of the child, life-survival-development, and respect for the child’s views. Compulsory state ownership is not a core principle.
tq: Find the unrelated institutional claim among principles stated in rights language.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s: The principle of respect for the views of the child is associated with which aspect of the UNCRC?
o: A condition for membership of the UN Security Council
A provision limited to armed conflict protocols
One of its four core principles
A financial provision for States parties
x: Respect for the views of the child is one of the four core principles of the UNCRC.
tq: Match the rights-based phrase with its proper conceptual category.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the Optional Protocols to the UNCRC?
1. Involvement of children in armed conflict — 2000
2. Sale of children, child prostitution and child pornography — 2000
3. Communications procedure — 2011
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The protocols concerning armed conflict and sale or exploitation of children were adopted in 2000, while the communications procedure protocol dates from 2011.
tq: Match each protocol with its subject and year before selecting the coded combination.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to India and the Optional Protocols to the UNCRC, consider the following statements:
1. India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005.
2. India is not a party to the 2011 Communications Procedure Protocol.
3. India ratified all three Optional Protocols in 2005.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005, but is not a party to the 2011 Communications Procedure Protocol. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
tq: Separate the two protocols ratified by India from the later protocol to which India is not a party.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Adoption of the UNCRC
B. India’s accession to the UNCRC
C. Adoption of the two Optional Protocols concerning armed conflict and exploitation
D. Adoption of the Communications Procedure Protocol
x: The sequence is 1989 adoption of the UNCRC, 1992 Indian accession, 2000 adoption of two Optional Protocols, and 2011 adoption of the Communications Procedure Protocol.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the 1992 and 2000 events between them.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Universal Children’s Day from India’s Children’s Day?
o: Universal Children’s Day is 14 November and India’s Children’s Day is 20 November.
Universal Children’s Day is 20 November and India’s Children’s Day is 14 November.
Universal Children’s Day is 11 December and India’s Children’s Day is 20 November.
x: Universal Children’s Day or International Child Rights Day is observed on 20 November, while India’s Children’s Day is observed on 14 November.
tq: Discriminate between two closely associated observance dates instead of merging them.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s:
Assertion (A): The UNCRC recognises participation as one of the broad categories of child rights.
Reason (R): Respect for the views of the child is one of the core principles of the UNCRC.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true. Participation is a broad rights category, while respect for the child’s views is a related core principle; the reason does not by itself explain the complete classification of rights.
tq: Check whether the true reason explains the full assertion or merely relates to it.
sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 24 — Prohibition of traffic in human beings
Article 39(e) — Duty of parents to provide education to children aged 6–14 years
Article 51A(k) — Fundamental duty of parent or guardian to provide education to children aged 6–14 years
x: Article 51A(k) makes it the duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to children between 6 and 14 years. Article 24 concerns child employment, Article 39(e) concerns protection of tender age, and Article 45 concerns early childhood care and education.
tq: Use the article-subject match and eliminate swapped constitutional provisions.
sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 39(e) requires that the tender age of children should not be abused.
2. Article 39(e) protects children from being forced by economic necessity to enter avocations unsuited to their age or strength.
3. Article 39(e) creates a fundamental duty upon parents to provide education to children aged 6–14 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 correctly describe Article 39(e). Statement 3 is incorrect because the parental duty to provide education is contained in Article 51A(k).
tq: Find the statement that assigns a neighbouring article’s subject to Article 39(e).
sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

s: Article 39(f), which concerns the healthy development of children in freedom and dignity and their protection from exploitation and abandonment, was reworded by the:
x: Article 39(f) was reworded by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. The 86th Amendment is associated with Articles 21A, 45 and 51A(k).
tq: Separate the amendment connected with Article 39(f) from the later education amendment.
sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

s: Which of the following constitutional provisions was substituted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment?
x: Article 45 was substituted by the 86th Amendment to provide for early childhood care and education until children attain six years of age. Article 51A(k) was added, rather than substituted, by the same amendment.
tq: Distinguish between a provision added by an amendment and one substituted by it.
sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

s: The Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016 provides that:
o: All work by persons below 18 years is prohibited without exception
Children below 14 years may work in any occupation after school hours
Children below 14 years cannot work, except for helping in family work after school, while adolescents aged 14–18 years are barred from hazardous work
Only employment in mines is prohibited for children below 14 years
x: The 2016 amendment prohibits work by children below 14 years, subject to the stated family-help exception after school. It also prohibits adolescents aged 14–18 years from hazardous work.
tq: Watch for extreme words such as ‘all’ and identify the age-group distinction.
sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

s: CHILDLINE 1098 is primarily intended to provide:
o: A portal for tracking school attendance
A legal aid service exclusively for women
x: CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24x7 emergency helpline for children. It is now integrated with ERSS-112 across all 36 States and Union Territories.
tq: Directly link the helpline number with its emergency function.
sec: Child helplines and portals → number/purpose

s:
With reference to child-protection helplines and portals, consider the following statements:
1. TrackChild is used for tracking missing and found children.
2. Khoya-Paya enables citizens to report missing or sighted children.
3. CARINGS is the Child Adoption Resource Information and Guidance System.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. TrackChild handles tracking of missing and found children, Khoya-Paya supports citizen reporting, and CARINGS relates to child adoption information and guidance.
tq: Match each portal with its distinctive purpose before selecting the coded combination.
sec: Child helplines and portals → number/purpose

s: Khoya-Paya has been integrated with which of the following platforms?
x: Khoya-Paya, the citizen portal for reporting missing or sighted children, has been integrated with TrackChild. ERSS-112 is associated with emergency response integration for CHILDLINE.
tq: Discriminate between similarly placed child-rights portals by their integration links.
sec: Child helplines and portals → number/purpose

s: e-Baal Nidan is associated with:
o: Online complaints regarding violation of child rights
Tracking children rescued from hazardous employment only
x: e-Baal Nidan is the NCPCR’s online complaint portal for violations of child rights. CARINGS is the adoption-related system, while CHILDLINE 1098 is the emergency helpline.
tq: Identify the portal by its institutional purpose rather than its name alone.
sec: Child helplines and portals → number/purpose

s: The composition of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights consists of:
o: Only a Chairperson and members nominated by the Supreme Court
A Chairperson and eight members, including three women
A Chairperson and six members, including at least two women
A Chairperson and four members, including one woman
x: The NCPCR consists of a Chairperson and six members, of whom at least two must be women. It is not composed solely of judicial nominees.
tq: Test the exact composition and the minimum representation requirement.
sec: NCPCR and SCPCR - parent Act, composition, powers, AP SCPCR

s: While inquiring into complaints, the NCPCR has the powers of a:
x: The NCPCR has powers of a civil court while inquiring into complaints. This power does not make it a constitutional or criminal court.
tq: Identify the exact legal status of the power instead of choosing a broader-sounding authority.
sec: NCPCR and SCPCR - parent Act, composition, powers, AP SCPCR

s: Which of the following Acts is NOT specifically included among those monitored by the NCPCR?
o: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
x: The specified monitoring mandate includes the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, the POCSO Act, 2012 and the RTE Act, 2009. The Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016 is not included in that stated list.
tq: Find the one law outside the commission’s specifically stated monitoring list.
sec: NCPCR and SCPCR - parent Act, composition, powers, AP SCPCR

s: In Andhra Pradesh, V. Gandhi Babu directed the admission of migrant and fisherfolk children into nearby schools and hostels in:
x: V. Gandhi Babu of the AP SCPCR directed admission-related measures for migrant and fisherfolk children in Kolleru in Eluru district.
tq: Combine the person, vulnerable groups and precise location in an applied current-affairs fact.
sec: NCPCR and SCPCR - parent Act, composition, powers, AP SCPCR

s: The National Policy for Children, 2013 defines a child as a person:
o: Between 6 and 14 years of age only
x: The National Policy for Children, 2013 defines a child as a person below 18 years of age. The 6–14 age range is relevant to the constitutional right to education, not the policy’s general definition of a child.
tq: Separate the policy’s general age definition from the RTE age group.
sec: National Policy for Children 2013 and National Plan of Action for Children - priority areas

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four priority areas of the National Policy for Children, 2013?
x: The four priority areas are survival, health and nutrition; education and development; protection; and participation. Military training is not a priority area of the policy.
tq: Recall the complete four-part list and eliminate the unrelated option.
sec: National Policy for Children 2013 and National Plan of Action for Children - priority areas

s: The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 primarily:
o: Introduced the constitutional right to education
Replaced the National Policy for Children, 2013
Limited child protection to the education sector
Operationalised the National Policy for Children, 2013
x: The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 put the National Policy for Children, 2013 into operation. It follows the same four priority areas.
tq: Distinguish an implementation plan from the policy it operationalises.
sec: National Policy for Children 2013 and National Plan of Action for Children - priority areas

s: Which principle is expressly associated with the National Policy for Children, 2013?
o: The best interests of the child come first
Education is the sole priority of child policy
Participation is limited to children above 18 years
The interests of institutions come before those of children
x: The National Policy for Children, 2013 places the best interests of the child first. Its framework also includes survival, health and nutrition, education and development, protection and participation.
tq: Apply the policy principle to a child-centred decision-making scenario.
sec: National Policy for Children 2013 and National Plan of Action for Children - priority areas

s: The Supreme Court decision in Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993) recognised that children below 14 years have:
o: A right to employment in non-hazardous industries
A statutory right to adoption under Article 24
A fundamental duty to provide education under Article 51A(k)
A fundamental right to free education under Article 21
x: Unni Krishnan recognised a fundamental right to free education for children below 14 years under Article 21. The decision formed the basis for the later insertion of Article 21A.
tq: Link the landmark case to the right and constitutional provision it developed.
sec: Child rights cases → issue

s: Which case upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, while excluding unaided minority schools from its application?
o: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
Unni Krishnan v. State of AP
Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India
x: Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India (2012) upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, but not in unaided minority schools.
tq: Discriminate between the two cases concerning RTE applicability to private and minority schools.
sec: Child rights cases → issue

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India held that the RTE Act does not apply to minority schools.
2. Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India concerned child trafficking and children working in circuses.
3. Bachpan Bachao Andolan later led to directions regarding registration of FIRs for missing children.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Pramati excluded aided and unaided minority schools from the RTE Act, while Bachpan Bachao Andolan addressed trafficking, circus children and FIRs concerning missing children.
tq: Combine case names with their distinct issues and check all three propositions.
sec: Child rights cases → issue

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Unni Krishnan v. State of AP
B. Constitution Amendment Bill relating to the right to education
C. Enactment of the 86th Constitutional Amendment
D. Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
x: The sequence is Unni Krishnan (1993), the Constitution Amendment Bill (July 1997), the 86th Amendment (December 2002), and Pramati (2014).
tq: Anchor the sequence with the case years and the 1997–2002 amendment milestones.
sec: Child rights cases → issue

s: According to the figures stated for child-related indicators, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Child sex ratio (0–6), Census 2011 — 914; NFHS-5 sex ratio at birth — 929
Child sex ratio (0–6), Census 2011 — 929; NFHS-5 sex ratio at birth — 914
Overall sex ratio, NFHS-5 — 914; child sex ratio, Census 2011 — 1,020

s: Which of the following correctly represents the NFHS-5 figures for IMR, U5MR and TFR, respectively?
x: The NFHS-5 figures stated are an infant mortality rate of 35.2, an under-five mortality rate of 41.9 and a total fertility rate of 2.0.
tq: Preserve the order of the three indicators while matching each figure.
sec: Child-related indicators - child sex ratio, child labour, AP figures

s:
With reference to child labour figures from Census 2011, consider the following statements:
1. Working children aged 5–14 years numbered about 4.35 million as main workers.
2. Including marginal workers, the total was about 10.1 million.
3. The figures refer exclusively to children aged 14–18 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The figures refer to working children aged 5–14 years, so statement 3 is incorrect.
tq: Check both the numerical values and the age range before selecting the coded answer.
sec: Child-related indicators - child sex ratio, child labour, AP figures

s: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by which Ministry of the Government of India?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
tq: Identify the ministry associated with the legislation rather than its implementing agencies.
sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

s: Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, which one of the following is correct regarding the definition of a child?
o: A person below 16 years, only if female
A person below 14 years, irrespective of gender
A person below 21 years, irrespective of gender
A person below 18 years, irrespective of gender
x: POCSO treats every person below 18 years as a child and applies in a gender-neutral manner.

sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

s: Under the POCSO Act, an offence committed by a person in a position of trust is treated as
o: an offence applicable only to institutions
x: The Act treats offences committed by a person in a position of trust as aggravated offences.
tq: Test the legal consequence attached to a special relationship of trust.
sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

s: Which one of the following is a feature of the special courts constituted under the POCSO Act?
o: They permit publication of the victim's identity after filing of the charge-sheet
They conduct trials only in public hearings
They transfer every case to a Children's Court
They provide child-friendly trials and keep the victim's identity secret
x: POCSO special courts are intended to conduct child-friendly trials and protect the identity of the victim.
tq: Select the option combining the two safeguards specifically associated with special courts.
sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the POCSO Act:
1. Section 19 deals with mandatory reporting of offences.
2. Sections 29 and 30 provide for presumptions against the accused.
3. The investigation is required to be completed within two months and the trial within one year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Section 19 concerns mandatory reporting; Sections 29 and 30 contain presumptions against the accused; and the prescribed timelines are two months for investigation and one year for trial.
